```{python}
import scanpy as sc
import pandas as pd
import scipy.io
from scipy import sparse
import anndata as ad
```

```{python}
d = "Wu_etal_2021_BRCA_scRNASeq/"   #folder namw

X = scipy.io.mmread(d + "count_matrix_sparse.mtx").tocsr()
genes = pd.read_csv(d + "count_matrix_genes.tsv", header=None)[0].values #selects the first column which is the genes 
cells = pd.read_csv(d + "count_matrix_barcodes.tsv", header=None)[0].values
meta = pd.read_csv(d + "metadata.csv", index_col=0)
```

```{python}
#to cehck if X is genes x cells
print(X.shape, len(genes), len(cells))
```

```{python}
#transpose X (AnnData wants cells x genes)
if X.shape[0] == len(genes):
    X = X.T.tocsr()
    
#AnnData is as a structured container for your single-cell experiment. 
#Instead of managing separate matrices and metadata files throughout the analysis, we have one object connecting them.
adata = ad.AnnData(X=X)
adata.obs_names = cells
adata.var_names = genes
adata.obs = adata.obs.join(meta)
adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()   # keep raw counts for pseudobulk
```

```{python}
#normalization adjusts for differences in total counts per cell. It does not eliminate every technical bias or prove that expression differences are biological.
#The values are now comparable on a common scale.
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4)

#After normalization, some genes can have very large values while many others have small values. This creates a highly skewed distribution.
#log1p() calculates:ln(1+x)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)

print(adata.obs.columns.tolist())
#adata.write_h5ad("wu2021_brca.h5ad")
```

```{python}
import numpy as np

adata = sc.read_h5ad("wu2021_brca.h5ad")

# 1. Look before filtering: exact labels and patient numbers
print(adata.obs["subtype"].value_counts())
print(adata.obs["celltype_major"].value_counts())
print(adata.obs.groupby("subtype")["orig.ident"].nunique())
```

```{python}
# 2. TNBC cancer epithelial cells 
mask = (adata.obs["subtype"] == "TNBC") & \
       (adata.obs["celltype_major"] == "Cancer Epithelial")
tnbc = adata[mask]

print(tnbc.obs["orig.ident"].value_counts())   # cancer cells per patient
```

```{python}
# 3. Sum raw counts per patient
X = tnbc.layers["counts"]
#Convert the sparse matrix to a regular array
X = X.toarray() if hasattr(X, "toarray") else X
#Attach gene names and cell identifiers
counts = pd.DataFrame(X, index=tnbc.obs_names, columns=tnbc.var_names)
#tnbc.obs["orig.ident"] provides the patient or sample identifier associated with each cell. groupby() groups cells with the same identifier, and .sum() adds their raw counts gene by gene.
pseudo = counts.groupby(tnbc.obs["orig.ident"].values).sum()
```

```{python}
n_cells = tnbc.obs["orig.ident"].value_counts().sort_index()
print(n_cells)

# Flag low-count patients
cutoff = 100
low = n_cells[n_cells < cutoff]
print(f"\nPatients under {cutoff} cancer cells:\n{low}")

# Quick look at the distribution
print(n_cells.describe())
```

```{python}
# 4. Log CPM
cpm = pseudo.div(pseudo.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 1e6
logcpm = np.log2(cpm + 1)
logcpm.to_csv("tnbc_pseudobulk_logcpm.csv")

# 5. Marker sanity check
markers = ["KRT5","KRT14","KRT17","EGFR","ESR1","GATA3","FOXA1"]
print(logcpm[[m for m in markers if m in logcpm.columns]].round(2))
```

A clear Basal-like tumor should show high KRT5/14/17 (and often EGFR) with low ESR1/GATA3/FOXA1. If a patient shows the opposite pattern, they are probably not Basal-like.

```{r}
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}

BiocManager::install("org.Hs.eg.db")
```

```{r}
library(genefu)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

# 1. Load the pseudobulk (patients x genes)
x <- read.csv("tnbc_pseudobulk_logcpm.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# 2. Map gene symbols to Entrez IDs (genefu's PAM50 uses Entrez)
entrez <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = colnames(x),
                 column = "ENTREZID", keytype = "SYMBOL", multiVals = "first")

#Keep genes that have valid mappings
keep <- !is.na(entrez)
x <- x[, keep]

#Create the gene annotation table
annot <- data.frame(probe = colnames(x),
                    Gene.Symbol = colnames(x),
                    EntrezGene.ID = as.numeric(entrez[keep]),
                    row.names = colnames(x))

```

The goal is to see whether the data contain enough of the 50 PAM50 genes to potentially classify samples into breast cancer molecular subtypes.

```{r}
# 3. How many of the 50 PAM50 genes are present?
data(pam50.robust)
#pam_ids contains the Entrez IDs associated with the PAM50 reference genes.
pam_ids <- pam50.robust$centroids.map$EntrezGene.ID
cat("PAM50 genes found:", sum(pam_ids %in% annot$EntrezGene.ID), "of", length(pam_ids), "\n")
```

```{r}
# 4. Call subtypes
pred <- intrinsic.cluster.predict(
  sbt.model = pam50.robust, data = x, annot = annot,
  do.mapping = TRUE, mapping = annot, verbose = TRUE
)
print(table(pred$subtype))
print(data.frame(patient = rownames(x), subtype = pred$subtype))
```
